Implementer's doubt (1), the 200->403 contract change, resolves in the change's favour rather than against it: real Mattermost returns 403 on insufficient permission for POST /teams/{team_id}/invite/email, so this moves TOWARD the repo's '/api/v4 compatibility' rule, not away. I re-ran the consumer search across the whole repo — the only hits for 'invite/email' outside router.go and the new test are two Go comments. No webapp, e2e, docs or OpenAPI consumer exists. Implementer's doubt (2), 'chi last-registration-wins was only observed via HTTP, never cross-checked against chi source', is now moot for review purposes: the RED run reproduces the exact symptom deterministically, so the behaviour is pinned by a test regardless of which chi internal causes it. Worth noting the mechanism is pinned empirically, not by a chi version constraint — a chi upgrade that started panicking on duplicate patterns would surface loudly, not silently.

I swept router.go for other duplicate method+path registrations (including with {param} names normalized, since chi matches by position not name) and found NONE. This was the only instance of its class; the fix is complete, not partial.

Checked the adjacent route for the same hole: /teams/{teamID}/invite-guests/email (inviteGuestsByEmail, compat_wave_handlers_final.go:1146) IS properly requireTeamAdmin-gated and registered once. No sibling leak.

legal/privacy (non-blocking, no attack path): restoring the gate also restores audit.LogAsync writing the submitted invitee email addresses into audit_logs — so this PR does increase personal data at rest versus the buggy status quo. Mitigating: it is the designed behaviour, the emails are caller-supplied, the purpose (security audit of an invite action) is legitimate, and audit reads (/audit/logs, /audits, /users/{userID}/audits at router.go:1156-1158) are inside a requireRole('system_admin') group. The real gap is pre-existing and out of scope: audit_logs has no retention or purge mechanism anywhere in the migrations or server/internal/audit. Worth a retention ticket, NOT a block on this PR.

Release note should say the behaviour change plainly: non-team-admins calling POST /api/v4/teams/{teamID}/invite/email now get 403 api.context.permissions.app_error instead of a false 200, and the call now leaves a team.invite.email audit row. Any out-of-repo integration that relied on the unconditional 200 will break — that is the intended fix, but it should not surprise anyone.

Next round: /teams/members/invite stays an ungated no-op stub returning 200 to any authenticated user, and the new test now pins that. Harmless today (inviteTeamMembersFromBody only guest-gates then writes {"status":"OK"} — no email dispatch, no state change), but if that stub ever grows real invite logic the test will happily keep asserting the ungated 200.
